zones.name: Low density residential zone
zones.purpose: The purpose of the Low density residential zone is to provide for: a. a variety of low density dwelling types, including dwelling houses; and b. community uses, and small-scale services, facilities and infrastructure, to support local residents. Precincts: Acreage, Large suburban, Small acreage, Small lot, Suburban, Village.
zones.typical: Dwelling house is accepted development; dual occupancy (auxiliary unit) is accepted subject to requirements; multiple dwellings need code assessment within precinct density limits (Table 5.5.5.1).

zones.name: Low-medium density residential zone
zones.purpose: The purpose of the Low-medium density residential zone is to provide for: a. a variety of dwelling types, including dwelling houses and low to medium density multiple dwellings; and b. community uses, and small-scale services, facilities and infrastructure, to support local residents. Precincts: Apartment, Townhouse.
zones.typical: Dwelling house is accepted development; multiple dwellings need code assessment; dual occupancy is accepted subject to requirements in the Townhouse precinct on 500 m² or more (Table 5.5.7.1).

zones.name: Medium density residential zone
zones.purpose: The purpose of the Medium density residential zone is to provide for: a. medium density multiple dwellings; and b. community uses, and small-scale services, facilities and infrastructure, to support local residents. Precincts: High rise, Medium rise.
zones.typical: Multiple dwellings (apartments) need code assessment; dwelling house is accepted development (Table 5.5.8.1).

zones.name: Emerging community zone
zones.purpose: The local government purpose of the Emerging community zone code is to protect the future use of land for urban purposes.
zones.typical: Dwelling house is accepted development; multiple dwellings are not listed in Table 5.5.3.1, so they are impact assessable.

zones.name: Rural residential zone
zones.purpose: The purpose of the Rural residential zone is to provide for residential uses and activities on large lots, including lots for which the local government has not provided infrastructure and services. Precincts: Carbrook, Cottage rural, Park living, Park residential.
zones.typical: Levels of assessment: not loaded yet – see Part 5.5 of the Logan Planning Scheme 2015.

rules.title: Flood hazard overlay
rules.code: 8.2.5 Flood hazard overlay code (with TLPI No. 1/2024)
rules.note: Part of the lot is mapped in the Flood hazard overlay. Development is assessed against the Flood hazard overlay code. Temporary Local Planning Instrument No. 1/2024 (in effect from 6 March 2025) changes the flood provisions and mapping, so use the TLPI version.
checklist: Read the Flood hazard overlay code as changed by TLPI No. 1/2024
Ask Logan City Council for flood information for the lot (Logan PD Hub)
Check for a newer TLPI on council's planning scheme page

rules.title: Acid sulfate soils overlay
rules.note: Part of the lot is mapped in the Acid sulfate soils overlay. Excavation or filling may need investigation and management under the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Acid sulfate soils overlay code
Check whether excavation or filling triggers the code

rules.title: Biodiversity areas overlay
rules.note: Part of the lot is mapped in the Biodiversity areas overlay. Clearing vegetation and siting buildings are assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Biodiversity areas overlay code
Map vegetation and habitat on the site plan

rules.title: Bushfire hazard overlay
rules.note: Part of the lot is mapped in the Bushfire hazard overlay. Siting, access, water supply and building construction are assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Bushfire hazard overlay code
Check the bushfire hazard category for the lot
Planning scheme policy PSP6 Bushfire hazard

rules.title: Extractive resources overlay
rules.note: Part of the lot is mapped in the Extractive resources overlay (resource area, separation area or transport route). Sensitive uses near extractive industry are assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Extractive resources overlay code

rules.title: Greenbank Training Area overlay
rules.note: The lot is mapped near the Greenbank Training Area (Defence). Development is assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Greenbank Training Area overlay code

rules.title: Heritage overlay
rules.note: A heritage place or area is mapped on or next to the lot. Demolition, alterations and new building are assessed against the Heritage overlay code.
checklist: Read the Heritage overlay code
Planning scheme policy PSP4 Heritage

rules.title: Landslide hazard and steep slope overlay
rules.code: 8.2.8 Landslide hazard and steep slope area overlay code
rules.note: Part of the lot is mapped as landslide hazard or steep slope. Earthworks and building are assessed against the overlay code; the Dwelling house code (AO27) also limits building height at the perimeter in these areas.
checklist: Read the Landslide hazard and steep slope overlay code
Get a geotechnical report if building on the mapped area

rules.title: Regional infrastructure and substations overlay
rules.code: 8.2.9 Regional infrastructure and substations overlay code
rules.note: Regional infrastructure (for example a major powerline, substation, pipeline or corridor) is mapped on or near the lot. Development near it is assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Regional infrastructure and substations overlay code
Check easements on the title

rules.title: Strategic airport environs overlay
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped airport environs area. Building height, lighting and noise-sensitive uses may be assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Strategic airport environs overlay code

rules.title: Water resource catchments overlay
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped water resource catchment. Development that affects water quality is assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Water resource catchments overlay code

rules.title: Waterway wetlands overlay
rules.note: A waterway or wetland (or its buffer) is mapped on the lot. Development and clearing near it are assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Waterway wetlands overlay code
Show the waterway or wetland and its buffer on the site plan

rules.title: Residential overlay (OM-10)
rules.code: Overlay map OM-10.00 Residential overlay; editor's note in Part 5.5 tables
rules.note: The lot is mapped as a residential area on overlay map OM-10.00. The Part 5.5 tables' editor's note says a Dwelling house here is accepted development subject to requirements, with the 9.3.2 Dual occupancy and Dwelling house code as the benchmark.
checklist: Check the Dwelling house against the 9.3.2 code's acceptable outcomes

rules.title: Transport noise corridor (OM-12)
rules.code: Overlay map OM-12 Transport noise corridors; QDC MP 4.4
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped transport noise corridor. Residential buildings in a designated corridor generally need noise-reducing construction under QDC MP 4.4 at building approval.
checklist: Ask the building certifier about QDC MP 4.4 for the corridor category

rules.title: Local plan
rules.code: Part 7 local plan code (the relevant plan) and Part 5.9 tables of assessment
rules.note: A local plan applies. Its tables of assessment (Part 5.9) can change the level of assessment set by the zone, for example in the Loganholme and Loganlea local plans.
checklist: Read the local plan code and its precinct for this lot
Check the local plan's tables of assessment in Part 5.9

rules.title: Water and sewer (Logan Water)
rules.note: New or intensified development needs water and sewer connection approval from Logan City Council (Logan Water) and may attract infrastructure charges.
checklist: Ask Logan City Council (Logan Water) about connections and services
Check for sewer mains through the lot (build-over rules, Dwelling house code AO17 / QDC MP 1.4)

zones.name: General residential zone
zones.purpose: The purpose of the General residential zone is to provide for the establishment of an appropriate mix of dwelling types, with small-scale community services for local residents. Precincts: Coastal communities, Suburban neighbourhood, Next generation neighbourhood, Urban neighbourhood.
zones.typical: Coastal communities and Suburban neighbourhood: dwelling houses (up to 15 dwellings per hectare, 8.5 m). Next generation: houses, dual occupancy and multiple dwellings (generally up to 12 m). Urban neighbourhood: multiple dwellings (8.5–27 m).
zones.source: City of Moreton Bay info sheet: General residential zone (MBRC Planning Scheme 2016)

checklist: Read the Riparian and wetland setbacks overlay code
Show the setback line on the site plan

rules.title: Heritage and landscape character overlay
rules.code: Part 8: Heritage and landscape character overlay code
rules.note: A heritage place, significant tree or landscape character area is mapped on or next to the lot. Demolition, alterations and tree removal are assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Heritage and landscape character overlay code
Planning scheme policy – Heritage and landscape character

rules.title: Scenic amenity overlay
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped scenic amenity area. Building height, bulk and siting may be assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Scenic amenity overlay code

rules.title: Extractive resources overlay
rules.note: An extractive resource, separation area or haul route is mapped on or near the lot. Sensitive uses are assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Extractive resources overlay code

rules.title: Infrastructure buffers overlay
rules.note: An infrastructure buffer (for example a powerline, pipeline, rail, sewage treatment or waste facility) is mapped on or near the lot. Development is assessed against the overlay code.
checklist: Read the Infrastructure buffers overlay code
Check easements on the title

rules.title: Transport noise corridor overlay
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped transport noise corridor. Noise-sensitive buildings may need acoustic treatment.
checklist: Read the noise provisions for the corridor
Planning scheme policy – Noise

rules.title: Building heights overlay
rules.note: The planning scheme maps the building height for this lot; the dwelling house and zone codes refer to it. See the mapped value in the layer attributes.
checklist: Check the mapped height in the layer attributes
Read the zone code's height outcome

rules.title: Walking distance overlay
rules.code: Overlay map – Walking distance (centre or train station)
rules.note: The lot is within a mapped walking distance of a centre or train station. This changes levels of assessment and densities for some housing (dual occupancy and multiple dwelling).
checklist: Check the walking distance overlay in the tables of assessment

rules.title: Community activities and neighbourhood hubs overlay
rules.code: Overlay map – Community activities and neighbourhood hubs
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped community activity or neighbourhood hub area, which the zone code refers to.
checklist: Read the General residential zone code and the Neighbourhood hubs info sheet

rules.title: Rural residential lot sizes overlay
rules.code: Overlay map – Rural residential lot sizes
rules.note: The minimum lot size for subdivision in the Rural residential zone is set by this map (2 ha, 6,000 m², 3,000 m² or no further reconfiguration).
checklist: Check the mapped lot size category in the layer attributes

rules.title: Road hierarchy / active transport
rules.code: Overlay map – Road hierarchy / Active transport
rules.note: The road or path network next to the lot is mapped. Access, frontage works and setbacks may be affected.
checklist: Check the road hierarchy and active transport maps

rules.title: Stormwater catchments overlay
rules.note: The lot is in a mapped stormwater catchment that sets stormwater management requirements.
checklist: Planning scheme policy – Stormwater management

rules.title: Local plan
rules.code: Part 7 local plan code (the relevant plan)
rules.note: A local plan applies (for example Caboolture West or Redcliffe Kippa-Ring). It can change zones' precincts, levels of assessment and lot sizes.
checklist: Read the local plan code and its precinct for this lot

rules.title: Temporary local planning instrument
rules.note: A TLPI is mapped on the lot. It overrides parts of the planning scheme while it is in effect.
checklist: Read the TLPI and check its expiry date

rules.title: Water and sewer (Unitywater)
rules.code: South East Queensland Water (Distribution and Retail Restructuring) Act 2009 – Unitywater connections
rules.note: New or intensified development needs water and sewer connection approval from Unitywater and may attract infrastructure charges.
checklist: Ask Unitywater about connections and services
Check for sewer mains through the lot (build-over rules)
